title: UPI, KYC and 'digital arrest' scams
summary: The scams hitting people in India right now, from fake KYC updates and UPI collect requests to 'digital arrest' video calls, and how to report them.
body_md:
## Why we cover personal scams at work

Scammers who get into your phone, UPI or email often get into work accounts next, and the same tricks are used on
businesses. Knowing them protects you, your family and the company.

## The common patterns

- **KYC update scams.** An SMS or WhatsApp says your bank, wallet or SIM will be blocked unless you update KYC
  through a link or app. Banks don't block accounts through messages with links.
- **UPI collect and QR scams.** You're told you'll *receive* money, then asked to scan a QR code or approve a
  request and enter your UPI PIN. **You never need your PIN to receive money.** Entering it always sends money.
- **"Digital arrest".** A video call from people dressed as police, CBI, customs or courier officials says a parcel
  or account in your name is linked to a crime, and that you're under "digital arrest" until you pay or transfer
  money for "verification". **No Indian agency arrests anyone over a video call or asks for money to clear your
  name.** Hang up.
- **Remote-access apps.** A "support agent" asks you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer or a screen-sharing app to fix
  a problem. Once installed, they can see your OTPs and banking apps.
- **Fake jobs and task scams.** Easy money for liking videos or rating hotels, followed by a request to "invest" to
  unlock earnings.
- **SIM swap.** Your phone suddenly loses signal: someone may have moved your number to a new SIM to receive your
  OTPs. Call your operator immediately.

## What to do

1. **Stop.** Fear and urgency are the scam. Real authorities give you time and written notices.
2. **Verify** using a number you find yourself (the back of your card, the official website), never one in the
   message.
3. **Never share** OTPs, UPI PINs, card CVVs or screen access.
4. **Report quickly.** Call the national cyber crime helpline **1930** or report at **cybercrime.gov.in**. The
   sooner you report a fraudulent transfer, the better the chance of freezing it. If a work device or account was
   involved, tell our security team too.

scenarios.body: Dear Customer your account will be suspended today. Update PAN/KYC immediately at hdfc-kyc-update.in to avoid blocking.
scenarios.explain: Banks don't suspend accounts through SMS links, and the domain isn't the bank's. Use the bank's own app.

scenarios.body: Hello sir, your courier from Mumbai customs contains illegal items. Join video call with Cyber Police officer now or arrest warrant will be issued.
scenarios.explain: This is the start of a 'digital arrest' scam. Block, don't join, and report on 1930.

scenarios.body: A payment of Rs 2,000 to Swiggy was made from your account. If this wasn't you, tap Report in the app.
scenarios.explain: A notification inside the official app about a transaction, asking you to act inside the same app, is the normal pattern.

quiz.q: Someone says they've sent you a refund and asks you to enter your UPI PIN to receive it. What's true?
options: You need the PIN to receive money
Entering your PIN sends money; it's a scam
It's safe if the amount is small

quiz.q: A video caller in uniform says you are under "digital arrest" and must transfer money for verification. What do you do?
options: Stay on the call and comply
Hang up; it's a scam. Report it on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in
Transfer a small amount to test
Share your Aadhaar to prove innocence

quiz.q: An SMS says your bank account will be blocked today unless you update KYC through a link. What should you do?
options: Ignore the link and check with your bank using its official app or number

quiz.q: Your phone suddenly shows "No service" and you didn't change anything. What could it mean?
options: Possible SIM swap; call your operator and bank right away

quiz.q: What is the national cyber crime helpline number in India?
